spiritual_reading:
# The
 Wheel
 Before
 the King of Honour:
 Spiritual
 Translation


---


**
¶1:** Again
 the
 teaching
 speaks
 concerning
 the comprehensive
 order
 of Divine
 Providence that stands
 perpet
ually before the Lord as governing Divine Good
,
 who
 dw
ells in the highest
 boundary between
 the natural and the
 spiritual mind
. This
 order
 is the
 in
most origin
 of every
 dominant selfish affection —
 both in
 the interior and exterior states of
 the natural
 man —
 held
 within
 a
 great and absolute
 restra
int. For
 the whole
 intention
 of the Lord
's
 governing
 wisdom
 operates
 through this order.
 And
 the
 entire opposition
 of evil affections throughout
 every
 state of the external mind is seized
 and held fast
 within it.

**¶2
:** This
 provid
ential order is rad
iant with divine
 wisdom, arranged in harmonious truths
 of
 sur
passing beauty. Now
, there are twelve governing
 principles
 within
 it —
 a
 full
ness of spiritual
 governance —
 and
 each principle
 stands
 between every
 state
 of the external mind and the dominant
 sel
fish tend
encies that inhab
it it. For
 should
 any evil
 aff
ection seek to evade divine
 order, it is bound
 fast
.
 Should
 it attempt
 fals
ification within its restra
int, that
 de
ception becomes manifest
 and exposed
 within
 this
 provid
ential arrangement
. All
 knowledges of good and truth,
 and
 the
 leading power
 among all spiritual forces, exist
 within
 it
 and are
 perfectly
 discerned through
 it
,
 in
 the presence of the
 Lord as
 governing
 Divine Good.

**¶3
:** The twelfth and
 completing
 principle within
 this order comprises
 the five
 essential perceptions of divine good — the
 spiritual senses — which are conjo
ined and interwoven throughout
 the entire sphere
 of the natural mind. For
 every state
 in
 which
 these
 perceptions are const
rained,
 and
 every state in which they have freedom,
 is displayed through
 this provid
ential order. The in
most origin
 of every external
 mental state,
 whether
 interior
 or exterior, and
 of
 every dominant selfish tendency
 within
 them
, is held and
 fixed within it
.

**¶4:** This
 perpet
ual divine
 perception is
 set
 at
 all
 times facing
 the Lord as
 governing
 Divine Good, so that holy
 awe —
 the rever
ential restra
int that proceeds
 from the
 Divine
 —
 may take
 hold
 upon
 all the com
mingled states
 where
 good and evil are not
 yet separated. Their
 in
most origin is fast
ened there, so that the
 evil
 within
 them cannot break
 free from the restraints of divine order
.

**¶5:** This
 provid
ential order
 is,
 in this respect, like
 a connected
 series
 of restra
ining
 tru
ths set
 before the inner
most governing
 principle of Divine
 Providence.
 For when any
 spiritual
 force
 moves
 within
 those
 interior
 states, it
 is held
 within
 that
 connected
 series.


**¶6:** So
 it
 is with
 every
 dominant
 selfish aff
ection dwelling
 in the external
 states
 of mind
,
 and with every force
 operating
 within the natural sphere:
 should
 they
 seek
 to ev
ade divine order, they are recognized
 and laid
 bare by this
 providential arrangement. For
 this
 order
 is like a great mirror of
 perfect self
-knowledge —
 the
 complete
 disc
ernment that separates good from evil
 and
 truth from falsity res
ides within it.

---

*
Note
 on
 "
five
 shining men"
 (
¶3
): This image
 is rendered
 as the
 five essential spiritual
 perceptions —
 corresponding
 to the five spiritual senses through
 which divine
 good is received
.
 The
 Ma
nichaean "
five light
some
 elements
" map
 closely
 to what
 Swedenborg calls the interior
 senses of
 the regener
ating
 mind
. The correspondence
 is strong
 but
 not without
 remainder
;
 these
 may
 also
 sign
ify five
 discrete
 forms
 of celest
ial good
 int
erwoven as
 one
 governing
 faculty
.*

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: [Agai]n the [teaching] speaks about the wheel that exists in front [of the King of Honour who dwells in] the seventh firmament [, and this wheel is], the root of the rulers above and below in a great and cruel fetter; as the entire will of the great King of Honour is placed in [it]. Also, their entire enmity, which is in the firmaments, is [seized] and ensnared in it.

It exists in a blaze of splendour [with] ornamentation and great beauty. Now, there are twelve seals in it. The seal between i[s] every firmament and the rulers who are there [, and all their powers,] are in it; for should one of them wish to escape, he will be bound [by the wheel]. If he should wish to cause a trick in his bond [, it will be] apparent and known in [that] wheel [before him]. The spheres and stars and [the] leader of all the powers exist there, and can be known by it, in front of the King of Honour.

The twelf[t]h seal that is in it is its five shining men that are conjoined and enmeshed through the entire zone; because every place where they are cramped, and every place where they have space, is displayed by that wheel. For the root of all the firmaments above and below, and that of their rulers, is ensnared and fixed in it.

The observation [of that wheel] is set right at all times opposite the great King o[f Honour who dwells in the seventh firmament,] so that fear, wh[ich proceeds from the King of Honour,] will assume all the powers of mixture [, and shall hold] their root affixed there, so that they cannot make an esc[a]pe from the fetter of their bond.
That wheel rese[m]bles, in this respect, a chain in front of the chief guard, for when [any power stirs] in th[ose firmaments, it is caught] in the [same cha]in.

This is also the case for all the rulers who are in the firmaments, and every power of the zone: If they should wish to escape, they shall be recognised and revealed by that wheel. [As] the wheel is like a great mirror, for [the di]scrimination of all things [above and below is] in it.
